answer: One concrete defence ties each identity to a scarce, rate-limited inlet: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must prove control of a unique verified channel, such as a hardware attestation or a bonded deposit. A sybil attacker can mint thousands of names, but each name needs its own inlet, so the attacker cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays only once. Cheap copies scatter like dust in a gale, while a genuine reputation grows slowly and verifiably, like a crystal adding one layer at a time.
